two-sum.clue: Find two distinct indices whose values meet a target.
two-sum.baseline: Try every index pair and add the values: O(n²) time, O(1) extra space.
two-sum.bottleneck: The same earlier values are searched repeatedly.
two-sum.optimal: Scan once, checking whether target minus the current value is in a value-to-index map before inserting the current value. The map represents only earlier indices, so one element cannot pair with itself.
two-sum.complexity: Expected O(n) time, O(n) extra space.
two-sum.edge: Duplicate values may form the pair; do the lookup before insertion.
two-sum.takeaway: Store what would complete the current candidate.

valid-parentheses.clue: Nested delimiters must close in reverse opening order.
valid-parentheses.baseline: Repeatedly remove adjacent matching bracket pairs until no change: O(n²) time, O(n) space for strings.
valid-parentheses.bottleneck: Each removal rescans most of the string.
valid-parentheses.optimal: Push opening brackets. Each closer must match the stack top; otherwise reject. An empty stack at the end proves every opening was closed in the right nesting order.
valid-parentheses.edge: Reject a closer with an empty stack and leftover openers.

merge-two-sorted-lists.clue: Two input chains are already sorted.
merge-two-sorted-lists.baseline: Collect values, sort them, and build a new list: O(N log N) time, O(N) storage, N total nodes.
merge-two-sorted-lists.bottleneck: Sorting rediscovers order already present in both inputs.
merge-two-sorted-lists.optimal: Use a dummy head and repeatedly attach the smaller front node. Every attached node is the smallest remaining, so the output stays sorted. Attach the remaining chain at the end.
merge-two-sorted-lists.complexity: O(N) time, O(1) auxiliary space when reusing nodes.
merge-two-sorted-lists.edge: One input can be empty; advance the pointer for the node just attached.
merge-two-sorted-lists.takeaway: Merge by preserving a sorted-prefix invariant.

best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock.clue: One purchase must precede one sale.
best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock.baseline: Try every buy/sell day pair: O(n²) time, O(1) space.
best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock.bottleneck: Each selling day repeatedly searches earlier minimum prices.
best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock.optimal: Keep the minimum price seen so far and the best nonnegative profit. At each sale day, that minimum is the best legal purchase; update the running minimum for later days.
best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock.edge: Decreasing prices return zero; never use a future minimum.
best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock.takeaway: Summarize the best legal past choice.

valid-palindrome.clue: A comparison ignores punctuation and letter case.
valid-palindrome.baseline: Build a normalized string and compare it to its reversal: O(n) time and O(n) space.
valid-palindrome.bottleneck: The filtered string is stored only to compare opposite ends.
valid-palindrome.optimal: Move two pointers inward, skipping non-alphanumeric characters and comparing case-normalized remaining characters. Everything outside the pointers has already matched.
valid-palindrome.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) extra space for the ASCII input contract.
valid-palindrome.edge: An empty normalized string is a palindrome; guard pointer crossings while skipping.
valid-palindrome.takeaway: Filtering can be performed during traversal.

invert-binary-tree.clue: Every node needs the same local transformation.
invert-binary-tree.baseline: Clone the tree with left and right subtrees exchanged: O(n) time, O(n) new output nodes plus O(h) recursion.
invert-binary-tree.bottleneck: A separate output tree is unnecessary when mutation is allowed.
invert-binary-tree.optimal: Swap each node's children and traverse both subtrees. Each local swap is independent, so applying it everywhere mirrors the tree.
invert-binary-tree.complexity: O(n) time, O(h) DFS auxiliary space, worst O(n).
invert-binary-tree.edge: An empty tree returns None; deep recursion may exceed Python's limit.
invert-binary-tree.takeaway: A whole-tree transformation can be a local recursive rule.

valid-anagram.clue: Character multiplicities must match, not merely membership.
valid-anagram.baseline: Sort both strings and compare: O(n log n) time, O(n) Python sorting space for equal lengths.
valid-anagram.bottleneck: Sorting computes order when only frequencies matter.
valid-anagram.optimal: Reject different lengths, then compare frequency counts. Matching counts for every character is exactly the anagram condition.
valid-anagram.complexity: O(n) time, O(A) space for alphabet size A; O(1) for fixed lowercase letters.
valid-anagram.edge: A set loses multiplicity, as in aab versus abb.
valid-anagram.takeaway: Choose counts when duplicates carry meaning.

binary-search.clue: A target is sought in a sorted random-access sequence.
binary-search.baseline: Scan every value: O(n) time, O(1) space.
binary-search.bottleneck: Sorted order can eliminate many candidates at once.
binary-search.optimal: Use a closed or half-open interval consistently. Compare the midpoint and discard the half that cannot contain the target; return its index only on equality.
binary-search.complexity: O(log n) time, O(1) extra space.
binary-search.edge: Two-element ranges expose off-by-one errors; use mid ± 1 with a closed interval.
binary-search.takeaway: Every boundary update must strictly shrink the search interval.

flood-fill.clue: Recolor a connected component in a grid.
flood-fill.baseline: Explore with a list of visited coordinates and linear membership checks: up to O((RC)²) time, O(RC) space.
flood-fill.bottleneck: Each visited membership test can rescan the component.
flood-fill.optimal: Save the original color and BFS/DFS through equal-colored neighbors, recoloring on discovery to mark visited. If original equals replacement, return immediately.
flood-fill.complexity: O(RC) time and O(RC) worst-case traversal space.
flood-fill.edge: Without the equal-color early return, mutation cannot mark discovery.
flood-fill.takeaway: A grid's neighbors define an implicit graph.

lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-searc.clue: BST order constrains where two nodes can meet.
lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-searc.baseline: Find both root-to-node paths then compare them: O(n) worst-case time and O(h) path space.
lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-searc.bottleneck: Paths are stored even though ordering tells which branch contains both targets.
lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-searc.optimal: If both target values are smaller, descend left; if both larger, descend right. The first split or target equality is their lowest common ancestor because no lower branch contains both.
lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-searc.complexity: O(h) time, O(1) iterative space; h may be n.
lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-searc.edge: This relies on the BST and guaranteed-present unique targets.
lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-searc.takeaway: Use structure-specific ordering before generic traversal.

balanced-binary-tree.clue: Every subtree must have child heights differing by at most one.
balanced-binary-tree.baseline: Recompute heights at every node: O(n²) worst-case time, O(h) stack.
balanced-binary-tree.bottleneck: Descendant heights are recomputed for each ancestor.
balanced-binary-tree.optimal: Postorder returns height or a failure sentinel. A failed child propagates immediately; otherwise compare child heights and return one plus their maximum.
balanced-binary-tree.complexity: O(n) time, O(h) stack, worst O(n).
balanced-binary-tree.edge: Checking only the root misses unbalanced descendants.
balanced-binary-tree.takeaway: Return the summary needed by the parent alongside validity.

linked-list-cycle.clue: Repeated node identity means a cycle.
linked-list-cycle.baseline: Store each visited node in a set: O(n) time, O(n) space.
linked-list-cycle.bottleneck: The set stores an entire traversal history.
linked-list-cycle.optimal: Advance slow by one and fast by two. In a cycle their relative distance changes by one modulo cycle length, so they eventually meet; without a cycle fast reaches None.
linked-list-cycle.edge: Compare node identity, not values; check fast and fast.next.
linked-list-cycle.takeaway: Different traversal speeds can reveal repeated structure.

implement-queue-using-stacks.clue: FIFO operations must be built using LIFO stacks.
implement-queue-using-stacks.baseline: Move all elements between stacks on every removal: O(n) per pop, O(n) space.
implement-queue-using-stacks.bottleneck: The same elements are reversed repeatedly.
implement-queue-using-stacks.optimal: Push into an input stack. Only when the output stack is empty, transfer all input elements into it. Each item transfers once before removal, amortizing the cost.
implement-queue-using-stacks.complexity: Amortized O(1) per operation, worst O(n) pop/peek; O(n) space.
implement-queue-using-stacks.edge: Do not transfer into a nonempty output stack, which would break FIFO order.
implement-queue-using-stacks.takeaway: Count total work over the lifetime of an element.

first-bad-version.clue: A monotone predicate changes from good to bad once.
first-bad-version.baseline: Query every version in order: O(n) API calls, O(1) space.
first-bad-version.bottleneck: A bad result also implies every later version is bad.
first-bad-version.optimal: Binary search the first true predicate over versions 1 through n. A bad midpoint remains a possible first bad version, while a good midpoint excludes itself and all earlier versions.
first-bad-version.complexity: O(log n) predicate calls, O(1) extra space.
first-bad-version.edge: The first or last version can be the boundary.
first-bad-version.takeaway: Boundary search preserves candidates rather than requiring equality.

ransom-note.clue: A source supplies a limited number of each character.
ransom-note.baseline: For each requested character, scan and remove a matching source character: O(mn) time, O(n) copied storage.
ransom-note.optimal: Count source characters, then decrement while consuming the note. A negative or missing count proves the note requires more than the source provides.
ransom-note.complexity: O(m+n) time, O(A) space, O(1) for fixed alphabet.
ransom-note.edge: Membership alone cannot satisfy repeated letters.
ransom-note.takeaway: Treat frequencies as a consumable resource.

climbing-stairs.clue: Each step count depends on smaller step counts.
climbing-stairs.baseline: Recursively branch into one-step and two-step choices: O(2^n) upper-bound time, O(n) stack.
climbing-stairs.bottleneck: The same remaining stair count is solved repeatedly.
climbing-stairs.optimal: The ways to reach i are ways(i-1)+ways(i-2), since every path ends in exactly one of those moves. Keep only the previous two totals.
climbing-stairs.edge: Define zero steps as one empty path when forming the recurrence.
climbing-stairs.takeaway: A recurrence follows from partitioning by the final choice.

longest-palindrome.clue: Rearrangement permits pairs around at most one center.
longest-palindrome.baseline: Enumerate ordered subsets and test each for a palindrome, keeping the longest: O(n!·n) upper-bound time, O(n) working space.
longest-palindrome.bottleneck: Order is irrelevant until letter pairs are counted.
longest-palindrome.optimal: Use every complete pair of each character; if any count is odd, add one center. No palindrome can use more unpaired centers, and these pairs are always arrangeable.
longest-palindrome.complexity: O(n) time, O(A) space, O(1) for fixed alphabet.
longest-palindrome.edge: Uppercase and lowercase letters are distinct.
longest-palindrome.takeaway: Prove both a counting upper bound and a matching construction.

reverse-linked-list.clue: Reverse a chain without indexed access.
reverse-linked-list.baseline: Collect node references then relink in reverse order: O(n) time, O(n) space.
reverse-linked-list.bottleneck: Stored references duplicate what pointer rewiring can preserve locally.
reverse-linked-list.optimal: Track previous, current, and saved next. Reverse current.next, then advance using saved next. Previous is always the head of the reversed prefix.
reverse-linked-list.edge: Save next before overwriting it; handle an empty head.
reverse-linked-list.takeaway: State the invariant of the processed prefix.

majority-element.clue: One value is guaranteed to occur more than half the time.
majority-element.baseline: Count occurrences separately for each value: O(n²) time, O(1) working space.
majority-element.bottleneck: Repeated scans count values that can be canceled against others.
majority-element.optimal: Boyer–Moore pairs different values away. Keep a candidate and balance; reset the candidate when balance is zero. A strict majority survives every cancellation.
majority-element.edge: Without a guaranteed majority, verify the final candidate in a second pass.
majority-element.takeaway: Cancellation can preserve the only possible winner.

add-binary.clue: Binary digits add with a carry from right to left.
add-binary.baseline: Pad strings and repeatedly prepend computed digits: O(N²) Python time, O(N) storage, N maximum length.
add-binary.bottleneck: Prepending copies the growing result each time.
add-binary.optimal: Walk both strings backward, adding available bits and carry. Append each output bit to a list, then reverse and join once.
add-binary.complexity: O(N) time, O(N) output buffer; O(1) state excluding output.
add-binary.edge: Process leftover carry and unequal input lengths.
add-binary.takeaway: Separate the constant-size arithmetic state from output construction.

diameter-of-binary-tree.clue: A longest path can pass through a node without starting at the root.
diameter-of-binary-tree.baseline: At each node recompute both subtree heights: O(n²) worst-case time, O(h) stack.
diameter-of-binary-tree.bottleneck: Heights are recalculated for many ancestors.
diameter-of-binary-tree.optimal: Postorder returns downward height. At each node combine left and right heights to update the best edge count, while returning only one downward branch to the parent.
diameter-of-binary-tree.edge: Diameter counts edges, and the best path may lie entirely below the root.
diameter-of-binary-tree.takeaway: The value returned upward can differ from the global answer.

middle-of-the-linked-list.clue: The middle position can be found without storing length.
middle-of-the-linked-list.baseline: Count nodes then traverse halfway: O(n) time, O(1) space, two passes.
middle-of-the-linked-list.bottleneck: The first pass's length can be represented by relative pointer progress.
middle-of-the-linked-list.optimal: Move slow one step and fast two. When fast finishes, slow is halfway through the list.
middle-of-the-linked-list.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) space, one pass.
middle-of-the-linked-list.edge: For even length, the standard fast=head rule returns the second middle.
middle-of-the-linked-list.takeaway: Relative speed can replace an explicit counting pass.

maximum-depth-of-binary-tree.clue: Maximum root-to-leaf depth combines child depths.
maximum-depth-of-binary-tree.baseline: Use BFS and count levels: O(n) time, O(width) queue space.
maximum-depth-of-binary-tree.bottleneck: No repeated work; the trade-off is the traversal frontier's size.
maximum-depth-of-binary-tree.optimal: DFS returns zero for an empty subtree and one plus the maximum child depth otherwise. Each node contributes once, using a path stack rather than a full level.
maximum-depth-of-binary-tree.complexity: O(n) time, O(h) DFS stack, worst O(n); BFS may be preferable for deep narrow trees.
maximum-depth-of-binary-tree.edge: An empty tree has depth zero; Python recursion needs care on skewed trees.
maximum-depth-of-binary-tree.takeaway: Choose traversal space based on tree shape.

contains-duplicate.baseline: Compare every pair: O(n²) time, O(1) space.
contains-duplicate.bottleneck: Each new element repeatedly scans its predecessors.
contains-duplicate.optimal: Insert values into a set, returning true if a value already exists. The set summarizes all previously seen values.
contains-duplicate.complexity: Expected O(n) time, O(n) extra space.
contains-duplicate.edge: Duplicates need not be adjacent; empty input returns false.
contains-duplicate.takeaway: Use a set when the count beyond one does not matter.

min-stack.clue: Minimum queries must remain cheap after push and pop.
min-stack.baseline: Scan the stack on every minimum query: O(n) query, O(n) storage.
min-stack.bottleneck: The current minimum of each prefix is rediscovered.
min-stack.optimal: Store each pushed value with the minimum through that depth, or use a second minimum stack with duplicate minima. Popping restores the previous prefix minimum automatically.
min-stack.complexity: O(1) per operation, O(n) extra space.
min-stack.edge: Repeated minima must survive one minimum being popped.
min-stack.takeaway: Cache the summary for each reversible state.

maximum-subarray.clue: The best contiguous sum can extend or restart at each index.
maximum-subarray.baseline: Enumerate all starts and extend running sums: O(n²) time, O(1) space.
maximum-subarray.optimal: Kadane's state is the best nonempty subarray ending here: max(value, previous+value). A negative prior contribution should be discarded; the maximum of these states is the answer.
maximum-subarray.edge: Initialize from the first value so all-negative input does not incorrectly return zero.
maximum-subarray.takeaway: An optimal prefix state can be sufficient for the next decision.

insert-interval.clue: Sorted disjoint intervals receive one new interval.
insert-interval.baseline: Append the new interval, sort, then merge: O(n log n) time, O(n) output.
insert-interval.bottleneck: Sorting repeats order guaranteed by the input.
insert-interval.optimal: Copy intervals strictly before the new one, merge every overlapping interval into its expanding boundaries, then append those strictly after it.
insert-interval.complexity: O(n) time, O(n) output space, O(1) extra beyond output.
insert-interval.edge: Touching closed endpoints overlap; the new interval may absorb all inputs.
insert-interval.takeaway: Exploit existing order to divide the scan into phases.

01-matrix.clue: Every grid cell needs distance to the nearest source of zero.
01-matrix.baseline: For each cell scan all zero cells: O((RC)²) time, O(1) work space beyond distance output.
01-matrix.bottleneck: Independent searches visit the same territory.
01-matrix.optimal: Start BFS with every zero at distance zero. The first arrival at any one-cell is its shortest path from the closest zero, since BFS expands all sources by distance together.
01-matrix.complexity: O(RC) time, O(RC) queue and distance storage.
01-matrix.edge: Mark on discovery, not removal; the input guarantees at least one zero.
01-matrix.takeaway: Many nearest-source queries can share one traversal.

k-closest-points-to-origin.clue: Only the k smallest distance values matter.
k-closest-points-to-origin.baseline: Sort all points by squared distance: O(n log n) time, O(n) sorting storage.
k-closest-points-to-origin.bottleneck: Full ordering of the n-k discarded points is unnecessary.
k-closest-points-to-origin.optimal: Keep a max-heap of at most k points using negated squared distances. When a closer point arrives, replace the farthest retained point; the heap always holds the k best seen.
k-closest-points-to-origin.complexity: O(n log k) time, O(k) heap space; k=1 gives O(n).
k-closest-points-to-origin.edge: No square root is needed; equal distances are allowed and output order is arbitrary.
k-closest-points-to-origin.takeaway: Bound the retained candidate set by the requested answer size.

longest-substring-without-repeating-char.clue: A contiguous substring must contain no repeated character.
longest-substring-without-repeating-char.baseline: Try each start and extend with a fresh set: O(n²) time, O(A) space.
longest-substring-without-repeating-char.bottleneck: Adjacent starts repeat most membership work.
longest-substring-without-repeating-char.optimal: Track each character's latest index. Move left to max(left,last_seen+1) on repetition, so the active window remains duplicate-free without moving left backward.
longest-substring-without-repeating-char.complexity: O(n) time, O(A) space for distinct characters.
longest-substring-without-repeating-char.edge: The max is essential on patterns such as abba.
longest-substring-without-repeating-char.takeaway: A window boundary records which past conflicts still matter.

3sum.clue: Find unique zero-sum triples without reusing indices.
3sum.baseline: Enumerate all triples, deduplicating answers: O(n³) time, O(K) answer storage.
3sum.bottleneck: For each first element, remaining pairs can use sorted order.
3sum.optimal: Sort, fix one value, and move left/right through the suffix according to the sum. Skip duplicate fixed values and duplicate matched endpoints to emit each triple once.
3sum.complexity: O(n²) time, O(n) Python sorting space plus O(K) output.
3sum.edge: Skip duplicate values, not all equal-valued indices before testing a valid triple.
3sum.takeaway: Reduce k-sum to a smaller ordered search.

binary-tree-level-order-traversal.clue: Results must be grouped by root distance.
binary-tree-level-order-traversal.baseline: DFS collects each node into its depth bucket: O(n) time, O(h) stack plus output.
binary-tree-level-order-traversal.bottleneck: No repeated work; BFS makes level boundaries explicit.
binary-tree-level-order-traversal.optimal: BFS with a queue processes exactly the current queue length per level. Children enqueued during that batch belong to the next level.
binary-tree-level-order-traversal.complexity: O(n) time, O(width) queue plus O(n) output.
binary-tree-level-order-traversal.edge: Handle empty root without enqueuing None.

clone-graph.clue: Copy identities and edges in a potentially cyclic graph.
clone-graph.baseline: Create clone list, then linearly find each edge's destination clone: O(V²+VE) time, O(V+E) clone storage.
clone-graph.optimal: Maintain original-node to clone-node mapping. Create a clone before visiting neighbors, then connect mapped neighbors. Early registration breaks cycles and preserves shared references.
clone-graph.complexity: O(V+E) time and clone output, O(V) auxiliary map/traversal space.
clone-graph.edge: Use node identity as keys, not merely values; self-loops must map to the clone.
clone-graph.takeaway: Memoization preserves identity as well as avoiding repeated work.

evaluate-reverse-polish-notation.clue: An operator consumes the most recent completed operands.
evaluate-reverse-polish-notation.baseline: Repeatedly replace evaluable token triples in a list: O(n²) time, O(n) storage.
evaluate-reverse-polish-notation.bottleneck: List scanning and shifting repeat after each reduction.
evaluate-reverse-polish-notation.optimal: Push numeric tokens. An operator pops right then left, computes their result, and pushes it; the stack contains evaluated expressions still waiting to be consumed.
evaluate-reverse-polish-notation.complexity: O(n) time, O(n) stack, under bounded integer arithmetic.
evaluate-reverse-polish-notation.edge: Subtraction/division operand order matters; truncate division toward zero, not floor.
evaluate-reverse-polish-notation.takeaway: A stack matches postfix evaluation order.

course-schedule.clue: Directed prerequisites must admit a complete ordering.
course-schedule.baseline: From every node search for a return to itself independently: O(V(V+E)) time, O(V) traversal space.
course-schedule.bottleneck: Reachability/cycle work is repeated across roots.
course-schedule.optimal: Use indegrees and Kahn's BFS: remove zero-indegree nodes and their outgoing edges. If all courses are removed, an order exists; any remaining graph contains a directed cycle.
course-schedule.edge: Include isolated courses; edges must point consistently from prerequisite to dependent.
course-schedule.takeaway: A dependency cycle is the obstruction to topological ordering.

implement-trie-prefix-tree.clue: Many strings share prefixes and both word/prefix queries are required.
implement-trie-prefix-tree.baseline: Store all words and scan on each query: O(NL) worst-case query time, O(total characters) storage.
implement-trie-prefix-tree.bottleneck: Queries compare the same shared prefixes repeatedly.
implement-trie-prefix-tree.optimal: Store characters as tree edges and mark terminal nodes. Follow one edge per query character; terminal distinguishes an exact word from a prefix.
implement-trie-prefix-tree.complexity: O(L) insert/search/prefix time, O(total inserted characters) nodes.
implement-trie-prefix-tree.edge: A prefix that exists is not necessarily a stored word; repeated insertion should be harmless.

coin-change.clue: Unlimited denominations form overlapping remainder subproblems.
coin-change.baseline: Try every usable coin recursively: exponential time, O(amount) depth for positive integer coins.
coin-change.bottleneck: The same remaining amounts occur via many coin orders.
coin-change.optimal: Set dp[0]=0; for each amount, minimize 1+dp[amount-coin] across feasible coins. Unreachable states stay infinite, so the minimum counts only realizable constructions.
coin-change.complexity: O(amount·C) time, O(amount) space for C denominations.
coin-change.edge: Return -1 for unreachable totals; amount zero needs no coins.
coin-change.takeaway: Specify whether the state minimizes count or counts possibilities.

product-of-array-except-self.clue: Each position needs a combination of everything except itself.
product-of-array-except-self.baseline: Multiply all other entries for each index: O(n²) time, O(1) work space plus output.
product-of-array-except-self.bottleneck: The same prefixes and suffixes are multiplied repeatedly.
product-of-array-except-self.optimal: Write left-prefix products into output, then sweep backward multiplying a running right-suffix product. Their product excludes exactly the current element and needs no division.
product-of-array-except-self.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary beyond O(n) output.
product-of-array-except-self.edge: Zeros invalidate total-product division; handle two zeros naturally.
product-of-array-except-self.takeaway: Combine summaries from both sides of an excluded position.

validate-binary-search-tree.clue: BST validity constrains all descendants, not just child pairs.
validate-binary-search-tree.baseline: Collect inorder traversal and check strict increasing order: O(n) time, O(n) list plus O(h) stack.
validate-binary-search-tree.bottleneck: The full traversal list is unnecessary for validating local order across the walk.
validate-binary-search-tree.optimal: DFS carries allowed lower/upper bounds. A node must lie strictly between them; recurse left with its value as upper bound and right with it as lower bound.
validate-binary-search-tree.edge: Duplicate values are invalid; a distant ancestor bound can be violated despite valid parent comparisons.
validate-binary-search-tree.takeaway: Propagate the global invariant into local checks.

number-of-islands.clue: Count connected land components in an implicit graph.
number-of-islands.baseline: DFS with a linear visited list: O((RC)²) worst-case time, O(RC) space.
number-of-islands.bottleneck: Visited lookup can rescan all prior land cells.
number-of-islands.optimal: Scan the grid; each unseen land cell starts one BFS/DFS that marks its entire component. Count starts, since no later start can belong to an already marked island.
number-of-islands.edge: Only orthogonal adjacency counts; mutation needs permission or a separate visited set.
number-of-islands.takeaway: Count components by counting new traversal roots.

rotting-oranges.clue: Spread occurs simultaneously in discrete minutes.
rotting-oranges.baseline: Scan the whole grid for new infections each minute using a snapshot: O(RC·D) time, O(RC) space for D rounds.
rotting-oranges.bottleneck: Cells far from the frontier are rescanned every round.
rotting-oranges.optimal: Multi-source BFS starts with all rotten oranges. Process one frontier per minute and decrement fresh count on discovery. If fresh cells remain after the queue empties, they are unreachable.
rotting-oranges.edge: No fresh oranges means zero minutes, including an initially empty queue.
rotting-oranges.takeaway: Simultaneous spread is a distance-layer traversal.

search-in-rotated-sorted-array.clue: A sorted array was rotated, but values are distinct.
search-in-rotated-sorted-array.baseline: Scan for the target: O(n) time, O(1) space.
search-in-rotated-sorted-array.bottleneck: One sorted half still permits elimination.
search-in-rotated-sorted-array.optimal: At each midpoint, identify which half is sorted. If the target lies in that half's value range, search it; otherwise search the opposite half. Distinct values make this test unambiguous.
search-in-rotated-sorted-array.edge: Include the correct boundary equality; duplicate-heavy variants need different handling.
search-in-rotated-sorted-array.takeaway: Find enough order to discard half, even without global order.

combination-sum.clue: Positive candidates can be reused to build a target.
combination-sum.baseline: Enumerate ordered coin choices to target, then deduplicate: exponential time, O(target/minimum) path plus outputs.
combination-sum.bottleneck: Different orders generate the same multiset repeatedly.
combination-sum.optimal: Backtrack with a start index, choosing only candidates at or after it; recurse with the same index to permit reuse. Sorted values allow stopping when a candidate exceeds the remainder.
combination-sum.complexity: Exponential search; O(C^(T/m)·T/m) loose upper bound, O(T/m) stack plus output; C candidates, T target, m minimum.
combination-sum.edge: Use the same index for reuse; positivity guarantees termination.
combination-sum.takeaway: Canonical choice order removes permutation duplicates.

permutations.clue: Every ordering of distinct values is requested.
permutations.baseline: Enumerate length-n sequences allowing reuse, then filter: O(n^n·n) time, O(n) path plus output.
permutations.optimal: Backtrack using a used set or in-place swaps. Extend only with unused values, so every complete path is a valid permutation and each appears exactly once.
permutations.complexity: O(n·n!) time including copies, O(n) auxiliary plus O(n·n!) output.
permutations.edge: Append a copy of the current path, not the mutable path itself.
permutations.takeaway: Prune invalid prefixes before completing candidates.

merge-intervals.clue: Unordered intervals must be united by overlap.
merge-intervals.baseline: Repeatedly scan all pairs and merge an overlapping pair: O(n³) loose upper bound, O(n) storage.
merge-intervals.bottleneck: Merged boundaries force more global rescans.
merge-intervals.optimal: Sort by start and compare each interval with the last merged interval. Once its start is beyond that end, no later interval can bridge back across the gap.
merge-intervals.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) Python sort/output storage.
merge-intervals.edge: Nested intervals need max end; touching closed endpoints merge.
merge-intervals.takeaway: Sorting turns arbitrary overlap into a one-pass frontier.

lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-tree.clue: No BST ordering can guide the search.
lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-tree.baseline: Build two root-to-target paths and compare: O(n) time, O(h) path/stack space.
lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-tree.bottleneck: The paths store more than the ancestor question requires.
lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-tree.optimal: DFS returns a found target or ancestor. If both children return nonempty results, the current node is the meeting point; if one does, propagate it. Target nodes count as their own ancestors.
lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-tree.edge: This assumes both targets exist; one target may be ancestor of the other.
lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-tree.takeaway: Combine evidence from two subtrees at their first meeting.

time-based-key-value-store.clue: Queries ask for the latest value no later than a timestamp.
time-based-key-value-store.baseline: Scan all versions of a key: O(k) per get, O(total versions) storage.
time-based-key-value-store.optimal: Store a timestamp/value list per key; set appends under the strictly increasing timestamp guarantee. Binary search the first timestamp greater than the query, then return its predecessor.
time-based-key-value-store.complexity: Amortized O(1) set, O(log k) get, O(total versions) space.
time-based-key-value-store.edge: A query before the first timestamp or an unknown key returns empty string.

accounts-merge.baseline: Compare every account pair for shared emails, then traverse the overlap graph: expected O(A²E) time with sets, O(AE+A²) storage; A accounts, at most E emails per account.
accounts-merge.bottleneck: Direct overlap checks repeat and do not immediately capture transitive membership.
accounts-merge.optimal: Map emails to accounts and union account indices sharing an email, then gather emails by component root and sort each group. Equal names alone never establish identity.
accounts-merge.complexity: O(M α(A)+M log M) upper-bound time, O(M+A) space; M email occurrences, A accounts.
accounts-merge.edge: Two different people may share a name; connectivity comes from emails.
accounts-merge.takeaway: Entity grouping is a connected-components problem.

sort-colors.clue: Only three known values must be partitioned in place.
sort-colors.baseline: Count each color and overwrite the array: O(n) time, O(1) space, two passes.
sort-colors.bottleneck: A second pass can be avoided when one-pass partitioning is required.
sort-colors.optimal: Dutch national flag keeps zero prefix, one middle, unknown range, and two suffix. Swap zeros left and twos right; recheck an element swapped from the unknown right side.
sort-colors.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) extra space, one pass.
sort-colors.edge: Do not advance the scan after swapping a two from the right.
sort-colors.takeaway: Multiple boundaries encode multiple settled regions.

word-break.clue: A string prefix may be segmented in several overlapping ways.
word-break.baseline: Recursively try every split without memoization: exponential time, O(n) stack plus substring copies.
word-break.bottleneck: The same suffix is tested after many prefix segmentations.
word-break.optimal: Let dp[i] mean the first i characters can be segmented. Try dictionary-word lengths ending at i, requiring a reachable prior boundary and exact word match.
word-break.complexity: O(n·L²) Python upper bound using substring hashing over lengths up to L; O(n+D) state/dictionary space, D dictionary storage.
word-break.edge: The empty prefix is reachable; greedy longest-word choice can fail.
word-break.takeaway: A reachable boundary is the reusable subproblem.

partition-equal-subset-sum.clue: Split positive values into two equal-sum subsets.
partition-equal-subset-sum.baseline: Enumerate all subsets: O(n·2^n) time with summing, O(n) working space.
partition-equal-subset-sum.bottleneck: Many subsets reach the same partial sum.
partition-equal-subset-sum.optimal: Reject odd total. Use boolean reachability up to half the total, updating sums downward for each value so each item is used at most once.
partition-equal-subset-sum.complexity: O(nS) time, O(S) space for half-sum S.
partition-equal-subset-sum.edge: Ascending updates would allow reusing the same element.
partition-equal-subset-sum.takeaway: Loop direction encodes one-use versus unlimited-use choices.

string-to-integer-atoi.clue: Exact lexical rules determine how a number is parsed.
string-to-integer-atoi.baseline: Try prefixes and repeatedly parse until invalid: O(n²) loose time bound, O(n) substring space.
string-to-integer-atoi.bottleneck: Previously scanned digits are parsed repeatedly.
string-to-integer-atoi.optimal: Skip leading spaces, read one optional sign, then consume consecutive digits. Accumulate numeric value and clamp to 32-bit limits, stopping at the first nondigit.
string-to-integer-atoi.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) extra space when accumulation is bounded by clamping.
string-to-integer-atoi.edge: Only leading whitespace is skipped; a sign without digits yields zero.
string-to-integer-atoi.takeaway: Turn the specification into explicit parsing states.

spiral-matrix.clue: Traverse each matrix cell in a rotating boundary order.
spiral-matrix.baseline: Walk with a visited grid and turn when blocked: O(RC) time, O(RC) visited space.
spiral-matrix.bottleneck: Visited state stores boundaries that can be summarized.
spiral-matrix.optimal: Maintain top, bottom, left, right boundaries. Traverse each remaining edge and shrink it, checking that a row/column still exists before traversing the opposite edge.
spiral-matrix.complexity: O(RC) time, O(1) auxiliary beyond output.
spiral-matrix.edge: Single rows and columns can be duplicated without boundary checks.
spiral-matrix.takeaway: A shrinking unvisited rectangle replaces per-cell state.

subsets.clue: Every subset of distinct values is needed.
subsets.baseline: Enumerate every length-n binary decision vector and scan selected elements: O(n·2^n) time, O(n) working space plus output.
subsets.bottleneck: All output subsets are necessary; recursive construction shares prefixes.
subsets.optimal: Backtrack over indices, recording the current path and extending only with later indices. Each subset has one increasing-index representation.
subsets.complexity: O(n·2^n) time/output upper bound, O(n) auxiliary stack.
subsets.edge: Include the empty subset and copy paths when storing them.
subsets.takeaway: Output size can set the unavoidable complexity floor.

binary-tree-right-side-view.clue: Only the last visible node at each tree depth is needed.
binary-tree-right-side-view.baseline: Collect all BFS levels, then take each last value: O(n) time, O(n) stored levels.
binary-tree-right-side-view.bottleneck: Full level contents are stored only to retain one item per level.
binary-tree-right-side-view.optimal: Use right-first DFS and record the first node encountered at a new depth. Earlier right-first branches dominate later branches at that depth.
binary-tree-right-side-view.complexity: O(n) time, O(h) stack plus O(h) output.
binary-tree-right-side-view.edge: A deeper node in a left subtree may still be visible; traverse both children.
binary-tree-right-side-view.takeaway: Traversal order can make the desired representative arrive first.

longest-palindromic-substring.clue: A palindrome mirrors around a center.
longest-palindromic-substring.baseline: Check every substring by comparing its ends: O(n³) time, O(1) validation space plus returned substring.
longest-palindromic-substring.bottleneck: Many neighboring substrings repeat symmetry checks.
longest-palindromic-substring.optimal: Expand outward from each odd and even center. Every palindrome has one such center, and expansion stops at the first mismatch.
longest-palindromic-substring.complexity: O(n²) time, O(1) auxiliary space beyond returned substring.
longest-palindromic-substring.edge: Even-length centers lie between characters; track indices rather than copying every candidate.
longest-palindromic-substring.takeaway: Enumerate structural centers instead of all intervals.

unique-paths.clue: Paths move only right and down in an obstacle-free grid.
unique-paths.baseline: Recursively branch on both moves: exponential time, O(R+C) depth.
unique-paths.bottleneck: The same cell-to-destination count is recomputed.
unique-paths.optimal: A cell's path count is the sum from above and left. Fill a one-dimensional row buffer, preserving the previous-row value until it is combined with the current left value.
unique-paths.complexity: O(RC) time, O(C) space, or O(min(R,C)) after choosing orientation.
unique-paths.edge: The first row/column has one path, not zero.
unique-paths.takeaway: DP dependencies determine a safe in-place update order.

construct-binary-tree-from-preorder-and-.clue: Preorder chooses roots; inorder splits left and right subtrees.
construct-binary-tree-from-preorder-and-.baseline: For each root linearly find its inorder position and copy slices: O(n²) worst-case time/space.
construct-binary-tree-from-preorder-and-.bottleneck: Index search and slicing repeat at each subtree.
construct-binary-tree-from-preorder-and-.optimal: Map unique values to inorder positions, consume preorder once, and recurse over inorder index bounds. The split size determines which values belong to each subtree.
construct-binary-tree-from-preorder-and-.complexity: O(n) time, O(n) index map plus O(h) stack and output.
construct-binary-tree-from-preorder-and-.edge: Values are unique; boundary errors can consume the next subtree's root.
construct-binary-tree-from-preorder-and-.takeaway: Represent subproblems with boundaries rather than copied slices.

container-with-most-water.clue: Area depends on width times the shorter of two heights.
container-with-most-water.baseline: Try every pair: O(n²) time, O(1) space.
container-with-most-water.bottleneck: Many narrower pairs share a height that already limits their area.
container-with-most-water.optimal: Start with widest endpoints. Move the shorter side because keeping it while reducing width cannot improve area; only a taller replacement can beat the current bound.
container-with-most-water.edge: Moving the taller side lacks the elimination proof.
container-with-most-water.takeaway: Discard a candidate only after proving its best future is no better.

letter-combinations-of-a-phone-number.clue: Each phone digit contributes one independent letter choice.
letter-combinations-of-a-phone-number.baseline: Enumerate strings over all mapped letters, then filter by positions: O(A^d·d) upper bound, O(d) working space.
letter-combinations-of-a-phone-number.bottleneck: Invalid position-letter combinations are generated unnecessarily.
letter-combinations-of-a-phone-number.optimal: Backtrack one digit at a time using only its mapped letters. Every leaf corresponds to exactly one valid combination.
letter-combinations-of-a-phone-number.complexity: O(d·4^d) upper-bound output time, O(d) auxiliary plus output.
letter-combinations-of-a-phone-number.edge: An empty digit input yields no combinations; digits are 2–9 by contract.
letter-combinations-of-a-phone-number.takeaway: Use local constraints to define legal branches directly.

word-search.clue: Find one word along a path without reusing cells.
word-search.baseline: Enumerate grid walks of word length and validate afterward: O(RC·4^L·L) upper bound, O(L) path space.
word-search.bottleneck: Most walks mismatch the word long before their last step.
word-search.optimal: Start DFS only on matching first letters. Match the next character before branching, mark the cell on the current path, and undo on return so other starts can reuse it.
word-search.complexity: O(RC·4^L) safe upper-bound time, O(L) path/recursion space using in-place marking.
word-search.edge: Visited is path-local, not global; restore the grid even on success.
word-search.takeaway: Backtracking state must describe one candidate path only.

find-all-anagrams-in-a-string.clue: All windows have exactly the pattern length and must match its counts.
find-all-anagrams-in-a-string.baseline: Sort each length-m window and compare with sorted pattern: O((n-m+1)·m log m) time, O(m) working space.
find-all-anagrams-in-a-string.bottleneck: Adjacent windows differ by just one outgoing and incoming character.
find-all-anagrams-in-a-string.optimal: Maintain counts for a fixed window and compare with the pattern counts. For a fixed lowercase alphabet, comparing 26 counts costs constant time per step.
find-all-anagrams-in-a-string.complexity: O(n+m) time, O(1) alphabet state plus O(K) result indices.
find-all-anagrams-in-a-string.edge: A pattern longer than the text gives no windows; duplicates require counts.
find-all-anagrams-in-a-string.takeaway: Fixed-size windows permit balanced add/remove updates.

minimum-height-trees.clue: Choose roots minimizing height in an undirected tree.
minimum-height-trees.baseline: BFS from every possible root: O(n²) time, O(n) space.
minimum-height-trees.bottleneck: Most traversals repeat the same distances.
minimum-height-trees.optimal: Repeatedly remove all current leaves until at most two nodes remain. Removing an outer layer reduces every interior root's height equally; tree centers survive.
minimum-height-trees.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) adjacency/queue space.
minimum-height-trees.edge: For n=1 return that node; this relies on a connected acyclic tree.
minimum-height-trees.takeaway: Peeling equal outer layers exposes the center.

task-scheduler.clue: Repeated task labels require cooldown gaps.
task-scheduler.baseline: Simulate slots, scanning all labels to choose the available task with highest remaining frequency, or idle if none is available: O((T+idle)·A) time, O(A) state.
task-scheduler.bottleneck: Idle slots are simulated even when only total length is requested.
task-scheduler.optimal: Let f be maximum frequency and c the number of labels with that frequency. The busiest tasks force (f-1) groups of cooldown+1 slots and a final c tasks; other tasks fill gaps. Answer max(T,(f-1)(cooldown+1)+c).
task-scheduler.complexity: O(T+A) time, O(A) counts; A=26 by contract.
task-scheduler.edge: Cooldown zero yields T; ties for maximum frequency affect the tail.
task-scheduler.takeaway: A bottleneck lower bound can become an exact constructive formula.

lru-cache.clue: Access and eviction both need constant-time updates.
lru-cache.baseline: Keep keys in a list ordered by recency: O(capacity) lookup/move, O(capacity) space.
lru-cache.bottleneck: List searches and shifts dominate every access.
lru-cache.optimal: Combine a key-to-node dict with a doubly linked recency list. On access detach and move to most-recent end; on capacity overflow evict the least-recent node and its dict entry.
lru-cache.edge: Updating an existing key also updates recency; remove evicted entries from both structures.
lru-cache.takeaway: Compose indexing and ordering structures to satisfy two operation needs.

kth-smallest-element-in-a-bst.baseline: Collect and sort all values: O(n log n) time, O(n) space.
kth-smallest-element-in-a-bst.bottleneck: Sorting ignores ordering already encoded by the tree.
kth-smallest-element-in-a-bst.optimal: Iterative inorder traversal counts visited nodes and stops at the kth. Left-node-right order yields exactly increasing values.
kth-smallest-element-in-a-bst.complexity: O(h+k) time, O(h) stack, worst O(n).
kth-smallest-element-in-a-bst.edge: k is 1-based; skewed trees can have linear height.
kth-smallest-element-in-a-bst.takeaway: Consume the natural sorted traversal only as far as needed.

minimum-window-substring.clue: A smallest variable window must cover character multiplicities.
minimum-window-substring.baseline: Try every substring and recount its characters: O(n³) upper-bound time, O(A) working space.
minimum-window-substring.bottleneck: Overlapping windows repeat counts and validity checks.
minimum-window-substring.optimal: Expand right, tracking unmet required multiplicities. Once all are covered, shrink left while valid, recording improvements. Removing a required occurrence makes the window invalid and resumes expansion.
minimum-window-substring.complexity: O(n+m) time, O(A) state for source length n and target length m, plus output.
minimum-window-substring.edge: Repeated target letters matter; empty or impossible targets need explicit handling.
minimum-window-substring.takeaway: Shrink a valid window to expose its minimal boundary.

serialize-and-deserialize-binary-tree.clue: A tree must round-trip including missing children.
serialize-and-deserialize-binary-tree.baseline: Serialize by recursive string concatenation with null markers: O(n²) worst-case time, O(n) text plus O(h) stack.
serialize-and-deserialize-binary-tree.bottleneck: Concatenation copies large subtree strings repeatedly.
serialize-and-deserialize-binary-tree.optimal: Append preorder tokens including a null marker to a list, then join. Deserialize by consuming one token per node/null in the same recursive order; markers determine the exact shape.
serialize-and-deserialize-binary-tree.complexity: O(n) token work and O(n) text/output under bounded-size values, O(h) stack.
serialize-and-deserialize-binary-tree.edge: Omitting null markers makes different tree shapes ambiguous; reject malformed external tokens.
serialize-and-deserialize-binary-tree.takeaway: An encoding must preserve structure as well as values.

trapping-rain-water.clue: Water above a position is bounded by maxima on both sides.
trapping-rain-water.baseline: For every index scan both sides for maxima: O(n²) time, O(1) space.
trapping-rain-water.optimal: Maintain left/right maxima and process the side with smaller current maximum. The opposite maximum already provides a sufficient upper bound, so the smaller side's trapped water is settled.
trapping-rain-water.edge: Ends trap no water; update the chosen maximum before adding its nonnegative water amount.
trapping-rain-water.takeaway: Finalize a quantity when one bound is guaranteed not to be limiting.

find-median-from-data-stream.clue: A growing stream needs median queries without full sorting.
find-median-from-data-stream.baseline: Append and sort on every query: O(n log n) query time, O(n) stored values.
find-median-from-data-stream.bottleneck: Each query rediscovers the partition around the middle.
find-median-from-data-stream.optimal: Keep a max-heap of the lower half and min-heap of the upper half, balanced within one element and ordered across the boundary. Heap tops then identify the middle one or two values.
find-median-from-data-stream.complexity: O(log n) insert, O(1) median, O(n) storage.
find-median-from-data-stream.edge: Balance sizes and cross-heap order; even counts need the mean of two tops.
find-median-from-data-stream.takeaway: Maintain precisely the partition needed by future queries.

word-ladder.clue: Minimum one-character transformations form an unweighted shortest path.
word-ladder.baseline: BFS scans all dictionary words for each visited word: O(N²L) time, O(N) traversal state.
word-ladder.bottleneck: Finding adjacent words repeatedly compares unrelated candidates.
word-ladder.optimal: Index words by one-position wildcard patterns. BFS visits compatible buckets and clears each consumed bucket, so their entries are not rescanned. BFS first arrival gives shortest length including the start word.
word-ladder.complexity: O(NL²) Python time and pattern-string storage, plus O(N) queue; N words of length L.
word-ladder.edge: The end word must exist; count words, not edges; clear buckets only after processing them.
word-ladder.takeaway: Separate neighbor discovery cost from traversal cost.

basic-calculator.clue: Nested parentheses and unary signs occur in a +/− expression.
basic-calculator.baseline: Repeatedly find and evaluate innermost parenthesized substrings: O(n²) time, O(n) copied text/stack.
basic-calculator.optimal: Scan once with current result, sign, and number. On an opening parenthesis push outer result/sign; on closing, combine the completed inner result with that saved context. Handle leading unary minus through sign state.
basic-calculator.complexity: O(n) time, O(depth) stack under bounded arithmetic.
basic-calculator.edge: Spaces must not reset a number; flush the final number and preserve the sign before parentheses.
basic-calculator.takeaway: A parser stack saves the enclosing computation context.

maximum-profit-in-job-scheduling.clue: Choose compatible intervals with different profits.
maximum-profit-in-job-scheduling.baseline: Enumerate job subsets and check overlap: O(n·2^n) time after sorting, O(n) working space.
maximum-profit-in-job-scheduling.bottleneck: Many subsets leave the same remaining suffix of jobs.
maximum-profit-in-job-scheduling.optimal: Sort by start time. For job i, compare skipping it with taking its profit plus dp[next compatible start], found by binary search. Compute suffix states from the end.
maximum-profit-in-job-scheduling.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space.
maximum-profit-in-job-scheduling.edge: A job ending exactly when another starts is compatible; greedily picking highest profit can fail.
maximum-profit-in-job-scheduling.takeaway: Weighted scheduling needs a state comparing future alternatives.

merge-k-sorted-lists.clue: Merge several already sorted node streams.
merge-k-sorted-lists.baseline: Scan all k list heads for each next node: O(Nk) time, O(k) head state.
merge-k-sorted-lists.bottleneck: The minimum head is rediscovered by a full scan.
merge-k-sorted-lists.optimal: Use a min-heap of one node per nonempty list. Pop the smallest, append it, and push its successor; each heap head is the next candidate from its stream.
merge-k-sorted-lists.complexity: O(N log k) time for k>1, O(k) auxiliary heap; reuse nodes, N total nodes.
merge-k-sorted-lists.edge: Use a serial tie-breaker so equal-valued nodes are not compared directly.
merge-k-sorted-lists.takeaway: A priority queue merges sorted streams incrementally.

largest-rectangle-in-histogram.clue: A bar's maximal rectangle extends until a shorter bar blocks it.
largest-rectangle-in-histogram.baseline: Try every interval, updating its minimum height: O(n²) time, O(1) space.
largest-rectangle-in-histogram.bottleneck: The same limiting bar is reconsidered across many ranges.
largest-rectangle-in-histogram.optimal: Maintain increasing-height indices. A smaller incoming bar finalizes each popped bar: its width runs from after the new stack top to before the incoming index. Flush with a zero sentinel.
largest-rectangle-in-histogram.complexity: O(n) time, O(n) stack, each index pushed/popped once.
largest-rectangle-in-histogram.edge: Equal heights need a consistent rule; the empty stack means the left boundary is before index zero.
largest-rectangle-in-histogram.takeaway: A monotonic stack waits until a boundary makes an answer final.
